Lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental programs in pediatric sarcomas nominate tumor-selective surface antigen pairs.

The authors analyzed a pan-pediatric single-cell RNA-seq atlas of 266 samples across 22 pediatric solid tumor types and found that these tumors express mixed neurodevelopmental gene programs reflecting their arrested progenitor origins. Categorization and analysis of 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency from single-cell RNA-seq data.

This review categorizes 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency (differentiation potential) from single-cell RNA-seq data into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based approaches. The authors analyze these methods under a unified mathematical framework, highlighting their differing assumptions and providing guidance for method selection. The work serves as a practical reference for researchers inferring cellular dynamics from static transcriptomic snapshots.

Denoising single-cell ATAC-seq data with Shannon entropy.

The authors introduce a Shannon entropy-based method for filtering low-quality droplets (empty, damaged nuclei, or debris) from single-cell ATAC-seq data. Unlike existing approaches that rely on read depth or predefined genomic features, this method uses the information content of the chromatin accessibility signal itself to distinguish high-quality nuclei. This improves downstream analysis by removing noisy droplets that can distort results and obscure rare cell populations.

CellWHISPER disentangles direct cell-cell communication from structural proximity.

CellWHISPER is a new computational framework for inferring direct, contact-dependent cell-cell communication (gap junctions and ligand-receptor signaling) from spatial transcriptomics data. It addresses a key problem in existing tools—high error rates caused by confounding spatial structure in cell types and gene expression—using a statistical procedure with closed-form significance scores that scales to large datasets.

Thermodynamic Quality Control Reshapes Spatially Resolved Metabolic Flux Predictions in Prostate Cancer.

The authors integrated spatial transcriptomics from twelve annotated regions of a single prostate tumor with a genome-scale metabolic model (Human-GEM) using an E-Flux framework, adding explicit thermodynamic cycle certification and loopless flux variability analysis. They show that genome-scale models can admit thermodynamically infeasible cycles (TICs) that distort spatially resolved metabolic flux predictions, and that applying thermodynamic quality control reshapes those predictions across normal, inflamed, and Gleason 3+3/3+4 tissue regions.

X-SPEAR: An Extensible Framework for Spatial Panel Evaluation and Refinement.

X-SPEAR is a framework for designing and evaluating targeted spatial transcriptomics gene panels, addressing the problem that genes chosen from scRNA-seq references are often detected in fewer cells in spatial assays, with gene-specific dropout. Its marker-selection method, DART, learns short Boolean gene rules and retains multiple gene-disjoint rules per cell type to improve rare-cell typing. This provides a systematic approach to panel design and quality control for platforms like 10x Xenium.

By combining a pan-cancer atlas of 318,426 cells and 78 cell types with survival data, they prioritize communication networks that have clinical relevance, revealing cancer-specific survival-associated interactions.

Deep-learning-driven tumor microenvironment profiling improves immunotherapy response prediction.

The authors present a deep-learning framework that profiles the tumor microenvironment by modeling structured, directional ligand-receptor signaling networks rather than relying on independent gene signatures or cell types. The work suggests that capturing multicellular communication structure, not just cell-type abundance, is key to forecasting clinical benefit.

Response to comments on "SpatialDG: a novel spatial domain identification method for spatially resolved transcriptomics data based on dual-graph neural network".

This is an author response addressing criticisms of SpatialDG, a dual-graph neural network method for identifying spatial domains in spatially resolved transcriptomics data. Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.

The authors propose a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, training a gradient-boosted meta-classifier on the raw scores from ten different inference methods (including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR, and ARACNe) so that method weighting varies by edge rather than being fixed globally. They also develop a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. Evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens, the approach aims to resolve disagreements between methods more effectively than picking one method or simple averaging.

Topology-adjusted knockout (TAKO): interpretable in silico single-gene knockout ranking on wild-type single-cell gene regulatory networks.

TAKO is a new computational framework that predicts the effects of knocking out individual genes using only wild-type single-cell RNA-seq data, without needing any knockout experiments for training. It works by building a gene regulatory network from the data and simulating gene removal through a 'cut-in-and-out' intervention on network dynamics, then ranking genes by how much their removal changes the network's steady-state behavior. This makes knockout impact prediction cheaper and more interpretable for single-cell studies.

Immune-chondrocyte ligand-receptor axes in osteoarthritis: microenvironmental control of inflammation, matrix remodeling, and chondrocyte fate.

This narrative review synthesizes evidence that osteoarthritis is a whole-joint disease driven by chronic low-grade inflammation, in which ligand-receptor communication between immune cells and chondrocytes translates microenvironmental cues into disease-relevant chondrocyte phenotypes. It catalogs major immune-derived or inflammation-amplified axes (e.g., IL-1β–IL-1R, TNF-α–TNFR) that regulate inflammation, matrix remodeling, and chondrocyte fate. The review frames these immune-chondrocyte interactions as central to OA progression rather than cartilage wear alone.

A curvilinear coordinate flatmap for visualizing hippocampal structure and development.

The authors developed a computational workflow that unfolds the curved, topographically complex hippocampal formation into a flat, planar map using curvilinear coordinates derived from solving the Laplacian equation. This flatmap preserves geodesic relationships and defines depth between meningeal and ventricular surfaces, enabling clearer visualization and analysis of subregional, laminar, and connectivity patterns in mouse hippocampal data registered to the Common Coordinate Framework.

A Spatial Multiomics Atlas and Resource for Immune-Fibrotic Niches in Chronic Kidney Allograft Dysfunction.

This study builds a cross-species spatial multiomics atlas of chronic kidney allograft dysfunction by combining a tacrolimus-modulated accelerated mouse model with human biopsy data, integrating single-cell/single-nucleus RNA-seq, flow cytometry, multiplex imaging, Visium HD spatial transcriptomics, and spatial metabolomics.
